section.sectionSummaryBrief: Preparation of the heart through bitterness before prayer is necessary for the arousal of the emotional attributes.
section.t: And he continues in the maamar,
(after explaining at length the concept of “from my flesh I perceive G-d”),
that in order for there to be an arousal of the emotions of the heart,
there must be preparation for this.
For although the arousal of the emotions of the heart comes through contemplation,
nevertheless,
in order for the light of the intellect to shine in his heart to arouse the emotions,
there must be preparation for this also from the side of the heart.
And this preparation is the bitterness that precedes prayer.
For by contemplating the ultimate descent of his soul below, which is a descent for the sake of an ascent,
that through its service in Torah and mitzvos it will ascend to a level higher than it was before its descent,
and how he actually conducts himself,
that not only does he not engage in Torah and mitzvos as required
(therefore the ascent of the soul through the descent is not complete),
but through his undesirable actions he brings his soul down even further,
and especially when he contemplates the parable of one who grasps the head of the king, etc.,
he will come to great bitterness.
And through this bitterness, the plowing of the ground of his heart is accomplished,
so that it becomes prepared for the arousal
(through contemplation)
of true emotions in the heart.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: In Elul, the revelation of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy enables even the most distant to prepare their hearts through bitterness, while also inspiring joy.
section.t: And he continues in the maamar,
that all this applies throughout the year,
and especially in the month of Elul, which is a time of revelation of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy,
and the revelation of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy in the month of Elul is for everyone,
even for those who are most distant.
Like the parable of the king in the field,
when anyone who wishes is permitted and able
to greet him
(and present their requests to him),
and he receives them all with a pleasant countenance and shows a smiling face to everyone.
[And one may add,
that although the explanation
(in the maamar)
of the advantage of the month of Elul comes in continuation of the matter of bitterness,

that since in Elul there is the revelation of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy even to the most distant, therefore it is a most opportune time to do plowing of the ground of one’s heart through bitterness,
the revelation of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy in Elul should also add in the matter of joy.
For since in Elul the king shows a smiling face to everyone,
this should arouse
(as water reflects a face back to a face)
an increase of joy in the service of the king].
And he concludes in the maamar,
that the explanation of “To you my heart says” — for you and in your place,
is,
that the heart is for Him, blessed is He, to fulfill His will, blessed is He, to make the lower world a dwelling place for Him, blessed is He,
and the explanation of “To you my heart says” — in your place, is the matter of the point of Judaism that exists in every single Jew, which is connected to the Awtsmoos.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Three interpretations of “face” in the verse correspond to worlds, souls, and G-dliness, explaining the two meanings of “To you my heart says.”
section.t: And to understand the explanation of the two interpretations of “To you my heart says,”
and their connection to the matters explained in the maamar
[the concept of “from my flesh I perceive G-d,”
and that in order for there to be an arousal of the emotions of the heart there must be preparation for this,
etc.]
one must preface what the Maggid said
in the name of the Baal Shem Tov, that in every word
of the words of prayer there are three levels,
worlds, souls, and G-dliness.
And based on this, one may also say regarding “Seek My face,”
that the service of “Seek My face” is in prayer,
which is in these three levels.
For in the word “face”
(in this verse),
there are three interpretations.
For according to Rashi’s interpretation of “To you my heart says,”
that the heart speaks in His agency or in His place, blessed is He,
“face” refers to His face, blessed is He,
the innerness of G-dliness.
And the Alter Rebbe interprets,
that this that the heart says “Seek My face” refers to its own innerness,
the innerness of the heart,
the innerness of souls.
And there is another interpretation of “Seek My face,”
that “face” refers to Atzilus,
for the four levels of face and back, right and left, are the four worlds of Atzilus, Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah
[back — Asiyah,
left — Yetzirah,
right — Beriah,
and face — Atzilus],
the innerness of the worlds.
